proof:
The affine gap $g_n$ is nonnegative on the sampled fibers, hence on $C$. The globally convex tests $\psi(n)e^{-t g_n}$ converge on $C$ to $\psi(n)\mathbf1_E$, dominated by the bound of $\psi$, giving the first inequality. On the domain $\ell>0$, $F(z,x)=\ell(z)\phi((x-y(z))/\ell(z))$ is a convex perspective composed with affine maps, so is convex. It admits a finite global convex extension agreeing on $C$: take the supremum of its affine supporting functions at points of $C$, whose slopes and intercepts are bounded since a compact neighborhood of $C$ is in the open positive domain. The extension is finite and continuous and equals $F$ on $C$. Use the admissible test $\psi(n)[F-t g_n]_+$ with that extension. On $C$ it converges to $\psi(n)F\mathbf1_E$ under a uniform bound, giving the second inequality.

For a fixed normal, approximate its singleton by continuous multipliers $0\le\psi_j\le1$ converging to its indicator. Dominated convergence restricts the second inequality to that normal. On each physical contact piece the change to pointed coordinates contributes $\ell(z)^{d-1}$ in surface measure, and the perspective contributes another $\ell(z)$. This yields the stated reference density and retains each fiber's response.
statement:
Let $C$ be the compact convex hull of the sampled fibers of a homothetic envelope $K_z\subset y(z)+\ell(z)D$, with $y,\ell$ affine and $\ell>0$ on the base hull. Use the summed fiber surface measure $dS$ lifted by the regular outer normal $n$. Suppose an integrable signed response $\Xi$ satisfies $\int\Phi\,\Xi\,dS\le0$ for every continuous nonnegative normal-dependent test that is globally convex in $(z,x)$ at each fixed $n$. Let $g_n(z,x)=n\cdot y(z)+\ell(z)h_D(n)-n\cdot x$ and $E=\{g_n=0\}$ on that bundle. For every nonnegative continuous $\psi$ on unit normals,
$$
\int_E\psi(n)\Xi\,dS\le0,\qquad
\int_E\psi(n)\ell(z)\phi\left(\frac{x-y(z)}{\ell(z)}\right)\Xi\,dS\le0
$$
for every nonnegative finite convex $\phi$ on $\mathbb R^d$. At a fixed facet normal of $D$, the pointed reference measure in the second inequality has density $\sum_z\ell(z)^d\mathbf1_{E_z}(\xi)$ relative to intrinsic facet area, with $\Xi$ still evaluated at each original fiber in its summand. Here $E_z$ denotes the contact subset at that normal, pulled back to the facet of $D$.
title: Convex physical tests localize to actual outer contacts through the perspective
